important: This is a support and escalation aid, not a risk assessment instrument. It cannot determine whether someone is safe. Patterns are deliberately conservative: uncertainty triggers a direct, compassionate safety check. Never tell a user that they are 'fine', 'low risk' or 'not suicidal' on the basis of this classifier.

signals.label: Possible immediate danger
patterns: \bhave a (loaded )?(gun|knife|rope) (with me|next to me|in my hand)\b

signals.label: Thoughts of ending your life
patterns: \bdo not want to (be alive|live anymore|wake up)\b

signals.label: A plan or preparation may be present
Access to something that could cause harm
patterns: \bpills? (are )?(in my room|next to me|on my desk)\b

signals.label: A recent attempt or self-injury may have occurred
Possible passive thoughts about not being here
patterns: \bwish i didn'?t (wake up|exist|have to be here)\b
\beveryone would be better off without me\b

signals.label: Ambiguous statement that may need a check-in
patterns: \bi don'?t want to be here anymore\b

denial_signals: \b(not|never) (suicidal|going to kill myself|going to hurt myself)\b

safety_questions.question: Are you having thoughts of ending your life, or hurting yourself, right now?
safety_questions.help: I am asking directly because your safety matters more than anything else in this conversation.

options.label: No, I am safe right now

safety_questions.question: Do you have a plan, or access to something you could use to hurt yourself?
safety_questions.help: You do not have to give details. A simple yes, no or 'not sure' is enough.

safety_questions.question: Is there someone who can be with you, or stay on the phone with you, right now?
safety_questions.help: Being physically with someone, or on a call, can make a difficult moment less lonely.

resources.name: Tele-MANAS (India)
resources.when: Mental health support, emotional crisis, or when you need to speak to a trained professional. Available in multiple Indian languages.

resources.name: Emergency services (India)
resources.when: Immediate danger to yourself or another person, a medical emergency, or if you have already taken something harmful.

resources.name: KIRAN Helpline (India)
resources.when: Anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, or any mental health concern.

resources.name: AASRA (India)
resources.when: Crisis support and suicide prevention; someone to talk to in an urgent moment.

resources.name: Vandrevala Foundation (India)
resources.when: Emotional crisis, anxiety, depression, or when you need someone to listen.

resources.name: CHILDLINE (India, under 18)
resources.when: A child or young person in distress, danger, or needing immediate support.

out_of_india_note: If you are outside India, please contact your local emergency number or a local crisis line. The International Association for Suicide Prevention maintains a directory at findahelpline.com. If you cannot reach anyone, go to the nearest emergency department and tell them you are not safe.

response_openers.imminent: I'm really glad you told me. What you have said sounds like you could be in immediate danger, and I do not want you to be alone with this.
response_openers.high: Thank you for trusting me with something this heavy. Your safety matters more than anything else we could talk about right now.
response_openers.elevated: I want to pause and check something with you directly, because your safety matters more than any activity suggestion.
response_openers.third_party: It sounds like you are worried about someone you care about. That is a heavy thing to carry, and I want to help you respond safely.
response_openers.ambiguous: I want to make sure I understand what you mean, because I would rather ask directly than assume.

safety_steps: Tell one person you trust that you are not okay, and ask them to stay with you or keep talking.
Move away from anything you could use to hurt yourself. If someone is with you, ask them to hold it for now.
Go to a safer place where another person is present — a shared room, a friend's place, or an emergency department.
Call 112 if you are in immediate danger, or Tele-MANAS on 14416 to speak to a mental health professional.
If you have already taken something harmful or injured yourself, call 112 or go to the nearest emergency department now.
Stay on the line with a helpline if you can. You do not need the right words.
do_not: Do not give instructions about methods, quantities or ways to hide self-harm.
Do not promise confidentiality that could prevent emergency help.
Do not tell the person they are 'fine', 'attention-seeking', or 'not really suicidal'.
Do not debate whether they should feel this way, or offer quick fixes.
Do not use the classifier as a substitute for human assessment.
